title: "Development"

This page is for people who want to change the app or build it themselves. The repository's [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD/blob/main/AGENTS.md) has the full contributor guide.

## How the app is put together

| Part | What it is | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Converter | A **Rust** library and command-line tool that reads the PDF with [pdf-inspector](https://github.com/firecrawl/pdf-inspector) and lopdf, builds the outline and writes the Markdown | `rust/converter/` |
| Desktop app | A **Tauri** app: a small Rust program that shows a web page (HTML, CSS and JavaScript) in the web view built into macOS, and calls the converter directly | `rust/app/`, `app/` |

**Rust** is a programming language that compiles to fast, self-contained programs. **Tauri** is a framework for desktop apps whose window is a web page; unlike Electron, which earlier versions used, it doesn't ship its own browser, which is why the app is about 6 MB instead of 110 MB.

The app and the command line call the same converter, so a conversion gives the same result either way.

## Running from source

You need **Rust** (install it from [rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs); it includes `cargo`, Rust's build tool), **Node.js 20 or newer** (a JavaScript runtime; it includes `npm`, its package installer, used here for the Tauri command-line tool and the tests), and **git**.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD.git
cd Petes-PDF-to-MD
npm install        # the Tauri command-line tool
npm run gui        # build and open the app
```

The first build downloads and compiles the Rust libraries and takes a few minutes; later builds are quick.

To convert from the command line:

```bash
npm run convert -- --input "path/to/document.pdf" --conversion-mode single
```

Options: `--out-dir <folder>`, `--conversion-mode single|major|sections`, `--include-section-metadata 0|1`, and `--out-subdir <folder>` (an extra folder level inside the PDF's folder).

## Tests

```bash
npm test            # builds the converter, then the smoke tests and the regression suite
npm run test:rust   # Rust unit tests, and the app's commands called the way the window calls them
```

The tests convert real PDFs and check the results, for example that footnotes aren't deleted, coded headings are found, two-column pages are read in order, and tables keep their words. The test PDFs live in `tests/pdfs/`, which is not committed to git; a test whose PDF is missing is skipped. The list of tests and the rules for adding one are in [`tests/TEST_PLAN.md`](https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD/blob/main/tests/TEST_PLAN.md).

## Builds and versions

```bash
npm run build:mac          # release build:  dist/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD-v1.0-macOS.dmg
npm run build:mac:debug    # debug build:    dist/Pete-s-PDF-to-MD-v1.0b-debug-macOS.dmg
```

The version is stored as `1.0.0` in `package.json`, the Rust `Cargo.toml` files and `rust/app/tauri.conf.json`, because those tools require three numbers. Users see **1.0**: a zero at the end is dropped.

Every build also moves to the next **revision letter** (`a`, `b`, …), stored as `buildRevision` in `package.json`. Release builds don't show it. A **debug build** does (`v1.0b`): it shows *(debug version)* in the window title and saves each conversion in a folder named after the build, for example `Annual-Report/v1.0b/`. Results from earlier builds stay in their own folders, which makes before-and-after comparisons easy. `npm run gui:debug` runs a debug build from source, and `npm run version:show` prints the current version.

## Releases

```bash
npm run release:prep -- --version 1.0.0 --build
```

This checks that `package.json`, the Rust crates, `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` all name the version, then makes a release build. Upload the DMG to a new release on the [Releases page](https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD/releases), tagged `v1.0`.

## The old version

The Electron app and Python converter used up to version 0.9 are kept, unmaintained, in `archive/electron-python/` in the repository. Its README says what each file was and how to check out the last version that used them.

## This website

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the `.qmd` files in `docs/`.

```bash
npm run docs:preview    # live preview in your browser
npm run docs:render     # build the site into docs/_site/
```

The Changelog page is copied from `CHANGELOG.md` when the site is rendered, so it never needs editing by hand.
